technical-data.invention-title: ADMISSION CONTROL OF MIXED VBR SOURCES IN BROADBAND NETWORKS
CONTROLE D'ADMISSION DE SOURCES VBR MELANGEES DANS DES RESEAUX A LARGE BANDE

abstract.p: In controlling the admission of variable bit rate (VBR) traffic, source classes are typically mixed in the sense that some can benefit from statistical multiplexing while others cannot. Moreover, such a mix of statistically multiplexable (S-VBR) and nonstatistically multiplexable (NS-VBR) sources is known to cause nonlinear interactions. Accordingly, if the boundary of the set of admissible connections is conservatively estimated by a linear approximation, the number of falsely rejected connections can become excessive. On the other hand, such an approximation permits admissibility to be easily decided in terms of the effective bandwidths of the traffic classes. Motivated by this background, the modified Chernov bound (MCB) is used to estimate the probability Psat of channel saturation and, with respect to a specified QOS bound on Psat, the set of admissible connections is formulated for worst-case regulated, periodic, on-off traffic. The S-VBR/NS-VBR dichotomy is characterized relative to this MCB-based admissible set and effective bandwidth computations are derived for S-VBR traffic. These results are then incorporated in an innovative, time-efficient admission control algorithm that applies to mixed S-VBR/NS-VBR traffic without compromising the accuracy of admission decisions. The algorithm relies on an ordering of classes according to their relative multiplexabilities along with a table of precomputed effective bandwidths for incremental values of residual capacity. The description of the invention concludes with an assessment of the algorithm's accuracy and computational efficiency as compared with alternative methods.

Lorsque l'on contrôle l'admission d'un trafic à débit binaire variable (VBR), on mélange généralement des classes d'origine de sorte que certaines d'entre elles peuvent bénéficier d'un multiplexage statistique contrairement à d'autres, ce mélange de sources statistiquement multiplexables (S-VBR) et de sources non statistiquement multiplexable (NS-VBR) pouvant causer des interactions non linéaires. Ainsi, si la limite de l'ensemble des connexions admissibles est estimé de manière raisonnable par une approximation linéaire, le nombre de connexions rejetées par erreur peut être excessif, cette approximation permettant néanmoins de fixer facilement l'admissibilité en ce qui concerne les largeurs de bande effectives des classes de trafic. C'est pourquoi l'on utilise la limite de Chernov modifiée (MCB) pour estimer la probabilité Psat de saturation du canal, l'ensemble des connexions admissibles étant formulé, par rapport à une limite QOS spécifique sur Psat, pour un trafic périodique par tout ou rien régulé dans le cas le plus défavorable. La dichotomie S-VBR/NS-VBR est caractérisée en fonction de cet ensemble admissible basé sur ladite limite MCB, et les calculs de largeur de bande effectives dérivés pour le trafic S-VBR. Les résultats sont ensuite incorporés dans un algorithme de contrôle d'admission à la fois innovant et efficace dans le temps, lequel peut être appliqué au trafic S-VBR/NS-VBR mélangé sans pour autant nuire à la précision des décisions d'admission. Cet algorithme repose sur une ordination des classes en fonction de leur multiplexabilité relative, ainsi que sur un tableau des largeurs de bande efficaces préalablement calculées, relatives aux valeurs incrémentielles de la capacité résiduelle. Cette invention concerne également l'évaluation de la précision et de l'efficacité algorithmique de cet algorithme par rapport aux autres procédés.

description.p: ADMISSION CONTROL OF MIXED VBR SOURCES IN BROADBAND NETWORKS
Technical Field

This invention concerns methods of connection admission control (CAC) for ATM networks, whereby requests for admitting and routing a virtual circuit are granted or denied on the basis of currently available network resources (buffer space in the nodes, channel capacity in the links) and quality of service (QOS) requirements. More in particular, the invention addresses a basic issue of recognized importance in the above context, namely how to guarantee QOS for multiplexed variable bit rate (VBR) sources, particularly when the the traffic classes are mixed with respect to their potential multiplexing gains. Background

A network in which the method of admission control and routing of requests for virtual circuits of the invention may be practiced is depicted in Figure 1. The means used to estimate both resource availability and prospective resource consumption
(by the requested circuit) is based on the concept of an effective bandwidth (EB).

In controlling the admission and routing of variable bit rate (VBR) traffic, source classes are typically mixed in the sense that some classes can benefit from statistical multiplexing while others cannot. Moreover, such a mix of statistically multiplexable

(S-VBR) and nonstatistically multiplexable (NS-VBR) sources is known to cause nonlinear interactions. Accordingly, if the boundary of the set of admissible sources is conservatively estimated by a linear approximation (for the purpose of determining
EBs), the number of falsely rejected connections can become excessive. This problem and certain difficulties associated with solving it are nicely described in the work of
Ewalid et al. [1]; its solution, however, is left open as a "subject of future work".

In a subsequent patent application by the same authors [2], they propose a step in this direction whereby bandwidth is allocated directly to CBR sources; available link capacity is then reduced accordingly and the EBs for the remaining classes are computed relative to this residual capacity. Although this approach can reduce the severity of nonlinear interactions, if the remaining VBR classes are mixed (which is likely) then the problem cited above persists. According to [1, 2], traffic sources are represented by worst-case, regulated rate processes. Object and summary of the invention

In view of this background, there is a need for innovative CAC methods that avoid the difficulties just mentioned. Moreover, if these methods are to profit from improvements afforded by the use of a modified Chernov bound (first considered by Hui [5] in this context), this requires a careful investigation of issues concerning multiplexability and effective bandwidth computation for the traffic classes in question.

In response to this need, the inventive methods disclosed in the section that follows feature a CAC algorithm which efficiently and accurately controls the admission/routing a diverse mix of ATM traffic demands, ranging from highly multiplexable S-VBR sources to nonstatistically multiplexable CBR demands. Innovative ancillary methods devised in the development of this algorithm include a means of ordering traffic classes according to their relative multiplexability, formulating lin- ear upper and lower bounds (hyperplanes) of an improved admissible connection region (based on the modified Chernov bound), and computing EB-entries for the table on which the CAC algorithm is based. The first section ( Case 1 ) considers the admissible set given by the modified Chernov bound (MCB) and, in terms of the traffic and resource parameters, derives necessary and sufficient conditions for class j sources to be S-VBR. The second section (Case 2) details the analysis and computations that accurately determine MCB-based effective bandwidths (EBs) when all classes are S-VBR. The third section (Case 3) responds directly to the need identified in the last paragraph of the background section, namely accurate admission control when the considered traffic is a mix of S-VBR and /NS-VBR classes.
The preferred algorithm of the invention is described in the section entitled "CAC algorithm for mixed traffic" (that is for Case 3).

Further testimony to the effectiveness of the TB algorithm has been obtained by evaluating its performance under simulated traffic conditions. Here, the nature of a newly arrived connection request is determined by randomly selecting its traffic class from a predefined set of S-VBR and NS-VBR classes. The latter include CBR 0 classes, where the probability ot a (.'BR connection is adjustable via a parameter of the simulation program. In the presence of such simulated traffic and for both the TB and SP methods, we evaluated channel utilization (relative throughput ). mean accepted bandwidth, and the probability that a connection is blocked ( not admitted). As revealed by Figure 8. which displays channel utilization as a func- 5 tion of the CBR-connection probability for both algorithms, the slightly improved performance realized by lengthy SP computations is barely perceptible. Moreover. with respect to the other two measures (accepted bandwidth, blocking probability) we have likewise found that the performance of these two algorithms is essentially identical.

However, as compared with the SP algorithm, execution of the TB algorithm is significantly faster. Indeed, together with accurate admission decisions, real-time implementation was a pivotal objective of the algorithm's development. By virtue

claim.claim-text: CLAIMS 1. Method of determining whether, in response to a request signal for a virtual circuit that routes variable bit rate (VBR) information through a network node with prescribed buffer and channel (output link) capacities, where the information source may be either statistically multiplexable (S-VBR) or nonstatistically multiplexable (NS-VBR), said request can be granted by said node, by an algorithm which, given the resulting traffic demand in terms of existing connections plus the requested connection, as represented by a vector describing the number of connections in each of plurality of J predefined S-VBR and NS-VBR classes, decides whether said connection vector is admissible with respect to a specified upper bound on the 0 probability of channel saturation, characterized in that the method employs a look-up table having J columns and K rows; the J columns correspond to the said predefined traffic classes and are listed in nonincreasing order of the extent to which a traffic class can benefit from statistical multiplexing; the K rows correspond to a quantization of the channel capacity C into K levels of residual capacity Ck=(k/K)C, where k=l,2....K, Ck being the capacity that remains available after prior allocations of bandwidth to NS-VBR connections and; letting Lk denote the largest class in said ordering of traffic classes, corresponding to the class S-VBR for a certain capacity Ck. the precomputed entry Ekj of row k, n column j of said look-up tables is
- if j>Lk, the maximum bandwidth required by class-j sources, class j being in this case NS-VBR for said capacity Ck; or

- if j≤Lk, the effective bandwidth of class-j sources as determined relative to all the Lk classes that are S-VBR for said capacity Ck. 2. The method of claim 1, wherein based on said look-up table and beginning with a capacity Ck=C(k=K) and traffic class j=J, the algorithm allocates bandwidth Ekj to any class-j connection in said connection vector and compares anaccumulated total allocation value b with C: if b>C, then said connection vector is not admissible; else if j>l and class j is S-VBR for the capacity Ck, where j<Lk, then the above allocation procedure is repeated for class j-1; else if j>l, then is k reduced to a value k', where Ck' is the residual capacity that remains after the class-j allocations, and the above routine is repeated for class j-1; else j=l and said connection vectors is admissible.

3. The method of claim 1, wherein each request signal from a certain traffic source has a set of leaky-bucket characterization parameters comprising a token rate parameter r regulating the average input rate, a token buffer capacity parameter BT defining the burst size and a peak rate parameter P defining the maximum peak rate of the source, the statistical multiplexability of a request coming from a source classified as belonging to a certain class of traffic being decreased in value by a factor corresponding to said parameter r, whereby a class nominally statistically multiplexable at a certain available bandwidth capacity of the link may result non- multiplexable because of said decrement of statistical multiplexability. and further characterized in that among requests classified as statistically multiplexable. a least- statisticallv- multiplexable request is identified as the one of highest class number that remains multiplexable after accounting for said decrement.

4. The method of claim 1, wherein for a set of traffic classes, all statistically multiplexable, the method comprises the computation of a linear upper bound (hyperplane) for the admissible set determined by the so-called modified Chernov bound (MCB) algorithm. 5. The method of claim 3, wherein the corner points of the MCB-determined admissible set are first determined algorithmically and then a linear outer bound is identified with the said hyperplane having the same corner points.
6. The method of claim 3, wherein a linear lower bound (hyperplane) for the MCB-determined admissible set tangent to a point on the boundary of said set is constructed.

7. The method of claim 5 whereby the tangent point is selected along a line that runs between the midpoint of the said outer bound and the original corresponding to the point where no sources are allocated; said tangent point being the point where this line intersects the MCB-determined admissible set and the construction of said linear lower bound (hyperplane) is based on partial derivatives associated with the MCB.
8. The method of claim 5, wherein effective bandwidths relative to a linear approximation of an admissible set of the traffic classes relative to the linear lower bound are computed.
